abundantly: they were abundantly supplied with food
acceptably: in an acceptable (but not outstanding) manner
accidentally: of a minor or subordinate nature
these magnificent achievements were only incidentally influenced by Oriental models
without intention; in an unintentional manner
accordingly: (sentence connectors) because of the reason given
across: the football field was 300 feet across
the marble slabs were cut across
actually: to be nominally but not actually independent
used to imply that one would expect the fact to be the opposite of that stated; surprisingly
you may actually be doing the right thing by walking out
the transmission screen shows the picture that is actually on the air
as a sentence modifier to add slight emphasis
actually, we all help clear up after a meal
afar: (old-fashioned) at or from or to a great distance; far
afresh: again but in a new or different way
afterward: happening at a time subsequent to a reference time
afterwards: happening at a time subsequent to a reference time
aimlessly: without aim; in an aimless manner
almost: (of actions or states) slightly short of or not quite accomplished; all but
along: we drove along admiring the view
in accompaniment or as a companion
his little sister came along to the movies
we sent them food and some clothing went along in the package
already: prior to a specified or implied time
always: at all times; all the time and on every occasion
I will always be there to help you
without variation or change, in every case
at any time or in any event
you can always resign if you don't like it
anew: again but in a new or different way
anywhere: at or in or to any place
you can find this food anywhere"; (`anyplace' is used informally for `anywhere')
apiece: to or from every one of two or more (considered individually)
aright: the flower had been correctly depicted by his son
around: by a circular or circuitous route
He came all the way around the base
used of movement to or among many different places or in no particular direction
wandering about with no place to go
in a circle or circular motion
arrogantly: in the old days she had been harsh and stiff; afraid of her husband and yet arrogantly proud that she had a husband strong and fierce enough to make her afraid
ashore: towards the shore from the water
assuredly: the grammar schools were assuredly not intended for the gentry alone
astray: away from the right path or direction
the arrow went wide of the mark
